subject: PlazaPay: sudden throughput collapse - path arbitration & firewall probe
messages:
From: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@plazapay.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@plazapay.com, sre@plazapay.com
Date: 2026-11-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: [INC] Major throughput collapse for /api/v1/charge - impact to checkout

Marissa —

We started seeing a ~75% throughput collapse on our checkout path around 08:50 PST. 5xx rate jumped from <0.5% to ~18%, median p95 latency increased 8x. This is affecting a subset of customers (us-west region) and blocking revenue flows. Our SRE team has captured tcp RST bursts and a Grafana snapshot attached.

Key observations from our side:
- Spike in TCP RSTs to redwood-proxy-usw2-*.redwood.net around 08:49:30
- Upstream retries and connection queueing on our side; backend services healthy
- DNS for api.plazapay.internal sometimes resolves to a deprecated gateway IP (older peering path)

We are elevating to PlazaPay execs and need a short remediation plan + ETA. Can you confirm whether Redwood saw any peering changes, firewall rule updates, or gateway restarts in us-west-2?

Attachments: plazapay-request-logs.zip, tcp-rst-snippet.txt, grafana-snapshot-09-05.png

--
Alice Barnes
Head of SRE, PlazaPay

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@plazapay.com>, sre@plazapay.com
Date: 2026-11-19T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: PlazaPay throughput collapse - preliminary triage

Quick triage notes (10:05 PST):
- Observed a transient route arbitration event in us-west-2 peering cluster at ~08:48:53. BGP metrics show a short-lived neighbor flap between pt-pek-2 and pt-usw2-3 that caused a routing preference flip for a /18 prefix used by PlazaPay egress.
- Firewall appliance logs (FW-EGRESS-PAY) show a sustained increase in SYN-ACK-to-RST ratios against the older gateway IP; we also see a handful of probes that look like health-checks hitting a stale NAT pool.
- DNS lookups from some PlazaPay client IPs returned an A-record with an older gateway IP (TTL 300). That explains asymmetric path where packets land at a proxy that has no active session for the modern backend pool and triggers TCP RST.

Actionable items I'm kicking off now:
1) Pin PlazaPay routes to the stable peering path (manual route preference bump) for the next 60m to stop flapping.
2) Push a firewall rule exception to allow PlazaPay CIDR through the newer proxy pool (targeted allow rather than global).
3) Ask PlazaPay to clear client DNS cache / lower TTL for api.plazapay.internal (we can push a short-term CNAME to the stable gateway).
4) Collect pcap from edge proxies and match RSTs to client IPs (already requested).

I'll attach the initial edge pcap excerpt and the routing diff once available. This looks like a peering-arbitration + stale-NAT issue rather than app regression.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: alice.barnes@plazapay.com
Date: 2026-11-19T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PlazaPay throughput collapse - mitigation plan and short-term ops

Adding a couple of pragmatic mitigation steps we can apply right away:
- Enable request-level retry smoothing and extend backoff window for PlazaPay route to reduce thundering retries. This buys us time while routes stabilise.
- Warm up a dedicated lightweight inference pool in us-west-2 (can spin up 4 reserved workers in 10-12 minutes) and move critical traffic there via header-based routing. This avoids the shared proxy NAT pool that was causing resets.
- We'll coordinate a rolling restart of the gateway proxies that returned to the deprecated IP set; restart will clear stale NAT entries.

Marissa: can you confirm exec briefing time? PlazaPay said they will bring CTO into the loop around 16:30 PST. If we have the temporary pool and firewall exception in place by 15:00 PST, we should be able to give a stable ETA to their execs.

Attachments: planned-warmup-steps.txt

—Neha
Support Engineering Manager

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@plazapay.com>, ops@plazapay.com, sre@plazapay.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-19T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: PlazaPay incident update & exec summary (planned mitigations)

Alice / PlazaPay leadership —

Summary (this afternoon): routing arbitration in our us-west-2 peering cluster caused a subset of PlazaPay traffic to be directed to an older gateway IP and a stale NAT pool. That mismatch produced TCP RSTs and downstream retries, leading to elevated 5xx and throughput collapse. No application code changes on Redwood or PlazaPay were detected.

What we have done / will do (ordered timeline):
- 10:05 PST: Identified peering flap and increased route preference for stable path.
- 10:20 PST: Applied a scoped firewall exception for PlazaPay CIDR to allow traffic through modern proxy pool.
- 11:00 PST: Requested PlazaPay to reduce DNS TTL and clear caches; provided a temporary CNAME to the stable gateway.
- 12:30 PST: Warmed a dedicated reserve pool and started header-based routing for critical checkout endpoints.
- 15:00 PST: Rolling restart of affected gateway proxies to clear stale NAT sessions.

Immediate impact: throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline by 15:20 PST, p95 latency back to within 1.5x baseline. We'll continue monitoring and push a full post-incident RCA by EOD tomorrow with packet-level evidence and timeline.

Next steps for execs:
- We recommend a short-term plan to reduce DNS TTLs for critical endpoints and a permanent route-pin policy for PlazaPay prefixes during maintenance windows.
- Proposal to add a dedicated small reserve pool for PlazaPay as a paid dedicated capacity option to avoid shared-NAT edge exposure (I will send pricing/contract options separately).

We will provide hourly status updates until we hand this back to standard support. Please confirm if you want a joint bridge at 16:30 PST for the CTO sync.

—Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
